Substituting numerical values: 1/R = 3; 1/(jωL)=1/(j·2·1/4)=1/(j/2)=-j2; jωC=j·2·3=j6. Therefore Y=3-j2+j6=3+j4. The voltage sine amplitude is 1, and the phase is taken as 0°, so the current phasor I=YV=3+j4, the magnitude |I|=sqrt(3^2+4^2)=5, and the phase angle θ=tan^(-1)(4/3)=53.1°. Therefore i(t)=5 sin(2t+53.1°).
